pages.title: Systems Skills | Jeremy Fontenot
pages.description: A task-based view of Jeremy Fontenot's professional IT support foundation and demonstrated junior systems administration capability.
pages.headline: Practical responsibilities connected to demonstrated capability.
pages.summary: This route organizes the portfolio by the work a junior administrator performs, then connects each responsibility to professional experience, personal-lab evidence, scope, and limitations.

sections.heading: Support identity records and access paths.
sections.summary: Professional support experience and lab evidence connect user symptoms to accounts, groups, roles, policies, authentication, and directory services.

cards.title: Maintain users and groups
cards.text: Create or update identity records under procedure, review membership and assigned roles, verify access state, and document changes.

cards.title: Support directory services
cards.text: Review domain structure, organizational units, users, groups, Group Policy, secure channels, and directory-service indicators.

sections.heading: Perform routine server, service, and virtualization work.
sections.summary: The evidence supports bounded administration tasks completed within documented procedures and escalation paths.

cards.title: Review server and service state
cards.text: Inspect roles, services, storage, event summaries, DNS, DHCP, logging, updates, and operational indicators.

cards.title: Support virtual machines
cards.text: Maintain inventories, review compute and storage state, inspect guest integration, and follow approved lifecycle procedures.

cards.title: Review cloud administration state
cards.text: Inspect tenant, identity, license, policy, application, sign-in, audit, and admin-center evidence within assigned permissions.

sections.heading: Automate, validate, document, and escalate.
sections.summary: The strongest job-readiness signal is the combination of technical work and safe operating habits.

cards.title: Run repeatable checks
cards.text: Use PowerShell for inventory, validation, structured export, sanitization, integrity checks, and repository quality.

cards.title: Review backup coverage
cards.text: Confirm scheduled scope, archive state, storage, supported integrity checks, controlled restore procedures, and cleanup.

cards.title: Escalate with evidence
cards.text: Separate confirmed results from inconclusive or untested conditions and provide observations, scope, commands, and next actions.

pages.scopeHeading: Ready to contribute within established controls.
pages.scopeText: The portfolio supports junior systems administration and infrastructure support readiness. It does not present personal-lab work as employer work or claim unsupported production ownership.

pages.title: Evidence Architecture | Jeremy Fontenot
pages.description: A recruiter-friendly guide to how portfolio claims connect to tasks, results, proof, provenance, scope, and limitations.
pages.headline: The skill comes first. The artifact verifies it.
pages.summary: This route explains how public claims connect to supporting artifacts without turning raw files into the main portfolio experience.

sections.heading: Five questions guide every proof relationship.
sections.summary: Recruiter-facing pages explain relevance before exposing raw artifacts.

cards.title: Skill
cards.text: What technical capability is being demonstrated?

cards.title: Task
cards.text: What administrative or troubleshooting work was performed?

cards.title: Result
cards.text: What was directly validated, configured, documented, inconclusive, or not tested?

cards.title: Proof
cards.text: Which public artifact, manifest, screenshot, export, script output, or report supports the claim?

cards.title: Scope
cards.text: What environment, access boundary, limitation, and unsupported conclusion must remain visible?

sections.heading: Existing proof surfaces remain available.
sections.summary: The architecture foundation adds a stable hub without replacing the established proof, dashboard, library, or case-study routes.

cards.title: Claim-to-artifact proof
cards.text: Primary recruiter-facing proof relationships and limitations.

cards.title: Evidence library
cards.text: Public artifacts, generated pages, preserved exports, manifests, and supporting records.

cards.title: Evidence status
cards.text: Relationships among validated, tested, configured, documented, inconclusive, and not-tested results.

cards.title: Home Lab case study
cards.text: System context, technical work, validation outcomes, and limitations.

sections.heading: Every migrated record will carry provenance and boundaries.
sections.summary: Later evidence phases must use the repository schema and migration contract rather than inventing new field sets.

cards.title: Source provenance
cards.text: Source repository, original path, source commit, integrity identifier, and collection context.

cards.title: Claim relationship
cards.text: Skill, task, result, supported claim, proof route, scope, and limitation.

cards.title: Publication classification
cards.text: Public original, sanitized derivative, metadata-only record, or source-reference-only entry.

pages.scopeText: Original artifacts remain preserved. Public presentation can use generated pages, summaries, or sanitized derivatives, but the source record and claim boundary must remain traceable.
